source_text: Ubi ergo me audisti sive legisti dicentem, "non innovari homines per Baptismum, sed quasi innovari; non liberari, sed quasi liberari; non salvari, sed quasi salvari"? … Non igitur ego inanem facio Dei gratiam: sed tu eius inimicus inanem quaesisse videris iactantiam, ut in tuam disputationem introduceres Epicurum, qui negavit esse corpus deorum, sed tamquam corpus, nec sanguinem, sed tamquam sanguinem … Quis autem nostrum dicit: "Quidquid in praesenti saeculo agitur, esse culpandum"
pass_a_gloss: Where then did you hear or read me saying 'men are not renewed through Baptism, but as it were renewed; not freed, but as it were freed; not saved, but as it were saved'? Not therefore do I make empty the grace of God: but you, its enemy, seem to have sought empty boasting, so that into your disputation you might bring Epicurus, who denied there to be a body of the gods, but as it were a body, nor blood, but as it were blood. But who of us says: 'Whatever is done in the present age is to be blamed'?
pass_b_english: Augustine reports, speaking to Julian: “Where, then, did you hear or read me saying ‘that people are not renewed through baptism, but as if renewed; not freed, but as if freed; not saved, but as if saved’?”

“It is not I, then, who make God’s grace empty; but you, its enemy, seem to have gone after empty display, so as to bring into your argument Epicurus, who denied that the gods have a body, but something like a body, nor blood, but something like blood …”
“But which of us says ‘that whatever is done in the present age is to be blamed’?”

choices.why: Keep the rite-name; Julian says praise of baptism is being used to smuggle natural evil.
Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-d): the old English summarised Augustine's report ('Augustine reports that Julian ...') instead of translating it. Now a translation of the Latin clause(s) that carry Julian's words or Augustine's report of them, with Augustine named as speaker where the words are his; nothing added that the Latin does not say. Omitted stretches inside a paragraph are marked with an ellipsis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row translates Augustine's report addressed to Julian, with Augustine named as speaker; Julian's words are the quoted parts.
kind: Julian allegations and an authority he invokes
